## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Uttarattheraapadāna* is a Pali verse biography located in the Therāpadāna section of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. According to commentary preserved alongside the verse tradition, the text describes the past-life meritorious deeds of the elder Uttara: during the dispensation of the past Buddha Sumedha, he was an accomplished sky-wandering wizard (*vijjādhara*) who beheld the Buddha radiating six-colored light from beneath a forest tree, descended to pay homage, and presented an offering of pure *kaṇikāra* flowers [Patton 2018].

Text-reuse analysis demonstrates extensive sharing of verse material between this work and the rest of Pali literature. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus registers 311 matching passages across 73 Pali texts, most prominently showing a near-complete alignment (§1.1–36.1) with the *Tikaṇikārapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 503), as well as significant correspondences with the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Rasavāhinī* [DharmaNexus]. Similar verse formulas are shared with other texts in the Apadāna corpus, including the *Sucintitattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 430), the *Pañcadīpikātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 9), and the *Pañcadīpadāyikātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 15) [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali, DharmaNexus detects automated alignments with the Sanskrit *Kaṭhināvadāna* and Tibetan canonical literature such as the *Vinayavastu* and the *Ārya-avalokana-mahāyāna-sūtra*, though these indicate shared stock phrases rather than curated recensional parallels [DharmaNexus].
